assumptions: Assay sensitivity (particle counter and capture assays) is sufficient to detect capture-positive co-localization at the fraction-level for the conditioned-medium yields available.
Exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer is orthogonally detectable and behaves comparably to endogenous EVs in capture and protection assays (assay-validation step required).
Device/formulation exposures tested are representative of intended clinical device and formulation envelope.
biological_rationale: MISEV2023 emphasizes orthogonal, membrane-protection and capture-based criteria to discriminate EVs from non-vesicular co-isolates. A surface-phenotype metric that (1) uses multiple capture epitopes, (2) is validated by an exogenous intact-EV spike-in and (3) is tested after realistic device/formulation exposures directly addresses whether surface-epitope masking or membrane disruption—rather than true loss of particles—explains variable capture signals and thereby enables treatment of surface-phenotype as a product-identity attribute.

candidate_quality_attributes.name: Spike-in-controlled intact-EV surface-phenotype (multi-epitope capture co-localized with particle peaks; detergent/protease-sensitive)
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: This attribute operationalizes a multi-epitope, membrane-protection-based surface-phenotype identity metric while controlling for assay recovery and buffer/device interference via an exogenous intact-EV spike-in.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: Moderate: depends on spike-in performance and capture-compatibility across formulation/device conditions.

edges.competing_explanation: Apparent loss of capture signal after device/formulation passage could reflect assay interference (capture reagent-buffer incompatibility) rather than true epitope masking or membrane damage.
edges.missing_experiment: Paired capture-compatibility controls for each formulation/device exposure and inclusion of exogenous spike-in tracer to rule out assay interference.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV recommends orthogonal capture and membrane-protection controls but does not specify device or excipient effects for this program.

edges.competing_explanation: Large-animal lack of detectable EV signal may be due to administration route or species clearance rather than device/formulation-induced masking.
edges.missing_experiment: Short-interval in vivo recovery tests with spike-in-controlled orthogonal capture to link in vitro device/formulation compatibility with in vivo detectability.
edges.model_or_species: context: non-human-primate evidence raises concerns about detectability after intranasal dosing
edges.uncertainty: High: macaque negative biodistribution highlights delivery/exposure risks that can be confounded by device/formulation-induced epitope loss; spike-in controls are required to interpret in vivo recovery.

nodes.statement: A multi-epitope immuno-capture signal (CD63/CD9/CD81 and TIM4/AnxA5) that co-localizes with particle-count peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive indicates a membrane-protected surface-phenotype distinguishing EV-enriched bounded fractions from secretome-retaining concentrates.

Passage through the candidate intranasal delivery device or contact with certain formulation excipient classes can mask epitopes or disrupt membranes, causing loss of capture-positive surface-phenotype despite similar bulk particle counts.

Including an exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer that is recoverable and membrane-protected in fraction-level capture validates assay recovery and discriminates true loss of endogenous EV surface-phenotype from assay or buffer interference.

If n1 and n3 are observed reproducibly after realistic device/formulation exposure, then the composite spike-in-controlled surface-phenotype metric can be adopted as a qualitative product-identity gate to progress an EV-enriched drug-substance candidate into CMC comparability and potency-development workflows.

competing_explanations: Loss of capture-positive signal after device/formulation passage reflects capture-reagent incompatibility or buffer interference rather than true loss of EV-associated surface epitopes.
Bulk particle-count similarity may mask conversion of intact EVs into non-membrane particles or debris that still register on NTA/TRPS, producing false equivalence in particle metrics.
dependencies: Establish or source a characterized exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer with orthogonal readout
Develop capture-compatibility buffer panels and SOPs for device rinse testing
Reserve device-shear simulation rig or representative clinical delivery devices
Secure >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots from the same source-cell bank/passage
design_question: Daily question: After passage through the candidate nasal delivery device and exposure to candidate formulation buffers, does an orthogonal intact-EV surface-phenotype workflow (multi-epitope immuno-capture + particle-peak co-localization + detergent/protease sensitivity) with an exogenous intact-EV spike-in control reproducibly discriminate EV-enriched bounded fractions from secretome-retaining concentrates as an identity metric (non-potency)?
expected_measurable_effect: Qualitative preservation (yes/no) of multi-epitope capture-positive co-localization with particle-count peaks in bounded fractions after device/formulation passage, validated by recovery of exogenous spike-in that is detergent/protease-sensitive. The expected effect is reproducible pass/fail identity calls across independent conditioned-medium lots.

experiment.assay: Orthogonal fraction-level workflow: (1) add exogenous spike-in to samples prior to device/formulation passage; (2) pass aliquots through device or device-simulating rig and incubate with each formulation buffer condition (matrixed); (3) fractionate resulting samples (iodixanol cushion or SEC) and measure particle counts per fraction to identify particle-peak fractions; (4) perform intact immuno-capture ELISA or bead-capture for each capture epitope on fractions and quantify capture signal for endogenous and spike-in tracers separately; (5) apply detergent + protease/RNase to captured material to test membrane-protection (signal loss indicates membrane protection); (6) run capture-compatibility controls for each buffer and device rinse.
experiment.comparator: Paired comparisons per conditioned-medium lot and per device/formulation condition: (1) EV-enriched bounded fraction passed through device + exposed to test formulation, (2) EV-enriched bounded fraction baseline (no device/formulation passage), (3) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining) passed identically through device + formulation, (4) concentrated conditioned medium baseline (no device/formulation passage). All samples are spiked identically with the exogenous intact-EV tracer prior to device/formulation exposure.
experiment.control: Positive controls: characterized small EV preparation (commercial or lab-validated) spiked and processed in parallel to verify capture and protection assay performance; Negative controls: buffer-only fractions and detergent-disrupted samples. Capture-compatibility controls: capture reagents incubated with each formulation buffer and device rinse to detect assay interference.
dependencies: Availability of consistent conditioned-medium lots (same source-cell bank/passage) for >=3 independent replicates
Access to a characterized exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer (distinct species or isotope-labeled) and validated capture reagents with known buffer-compatibility
Device-shear characterization or representative clinical device(s) to simulate passage
Particle-count instrumentation (NTA or TRPS) and fractionation capability (iodixanol or SEC)
Laboratory capacity for capture, protection assays, and compatibility testing
experiment.failure_criterion: Either (A) validated spike-in tracer shows membrane-protected recovery but endogenous multi-epitope capture-positive co-localization is not reproducibly observed in bounded fractions after device/formulation passage across independent lots (n  3), falsifying the identity gate; or (B) capture-compatibility controls indicate observed capture-signal loss is explained entirely by capture reagent/formulation incompatibility, preventing discrimination of true epitope masking from assay interference.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If falsified (and assay controls confirm spike-in recovery and rule out reagent incompatibility), the program must treat the preparation as indistinguishable from secretome for product-identity purposes and deprioritize a surface-phenotype identity gate; proceed to alternative identity attributes (e.g., protected-cargo fingerprint or spike-in-protected fractionation gates) or revise fractionation/formulation/device strategy. If falsification is due to assay interference, revise capture reagents or buffer formulations and repeat the controlled test.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: A multi-epitope immuno-capture surface-phenotype (CD63/CD9/CD81 and TIM4/AnxA5) that co-localizes with particle-count peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive will be preserved in EV-enriched bounded fractions after device/formulation passage and validated by recovery of an exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer; concentrated secretome-retaining concentrates will either lack this co-localized, membrane-protected surface-phenotype or will show capture-signal that is insensitive to detergent/protease.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative pass/fail for each lot/condition: (A) particle-count peak(s) co-localize with multi-epitope capture-positive signal (yes/no) in bounded fractions after device/formulation passage, (B) exogenous spike-in tracer recovery in those capture-positive, particle-peak fractions is observed and lost after detergent + protease/RNase (validating assay recovery and membrane protection), and (C) endogenous capture signal in secretome-retaining concentrates is absent or detergent-insensitive. The overall primary readout is a reproducible qualitative identity call (EV-enriched pass vs secretome fail) across independent lots.
experiment.question: Does a multi-epitope, spike-in-controlled intact-EV surface-phenotype assay preserve capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks after realistic device/formulation passage, distinguishing EV-enriched bounded fractions from secretome-retaining concentrates?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium (same source-cell lot) processed into: (A) EV-enriched bounded fraction (program-defined fractionation) and (B) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining) from the same lot
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in tracer (orthogonal species or isotope-labeled) with verified marker display and particle count for within-sample recovery control
Panel of capture reagents: anti-CD63, anti-CD9, anti-CD81, TIM4 or AnxA5 capture reagents (intact-capture formats) and reagent compatibility buffers
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents for fraction-level particle counts
Protease (proteinase K) and RNase reagents and detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent) for membrane-disruption tests
Density-gradient materials (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors
Representative nasal-delivery device(s) or device-flow rigs to simulate clinical passage and device rinse solutions
A panel of candidate formulation buffers/excipient classes to test (matrix across pH/ionic strength/non-ionic surfactant presence) and baseline control buffer
Buffers and blocking reagents for capture assays and capture-compatibility controls
secondary_readouts: Capture-compatibility panel results per formulation buffer (evidence of assay interference vs true signal loss)
Per-fraction protein:particle ratio comparisons between bounded fractions and secretome controls
Spike-in recovery percentage per fraction (qualitative recovered & membrane-protected vs not recovered)
Reproducibility across biological replicates (n  3 conditioned-medium lots)
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: Across >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots, for >=1 formulation/device condition representative of intended clinical use, the bounded EV-enriched fraction after device/formulation passage shows: (1) particle-peak co-localization with multi-epitope capture-positive signal; (2) recovered exogenous spike-in tracer in the same fractions with detergent/protease-sensitive behavior (loss after disruption); (3) endogenous capture-positive signal that is substantially reduced or abolished after detergent + protease/RNase, while concentrated secretome-retaining controls processed identically lack co-localized, detergent-sensitive capture signal. Capture-compatibility controls confirm that observed signal loss is not due to assay reagent-buffer interference.

explicit_inferences: Inference: Capture-signal loss can arise from true membrane disruption, epitope masking by excipients, or capture-assay incompatibility; inclusion of spike-in tracer and capture-compatibility panels distinguishes these possibilities.

Inference: Demonstrating preserved spike-in-protected recovery plus preserved endogenous multi-epitope capture co-localization after device/formulation passage supports adopting surface-phenotype as a qualitative identity gate; failure to demonstrate this requires treating material as secretome-like for identity and CMC planning.
falsification_criteria: Validated spike-in tracer is recovered and demonstrates membrane-protection behavior (loss after detergent + protease), but endogenous multi-epitope capture-positive signal that co-localizes with particle-peak fractions is not reproducibly observed in bounded fractions after device/formulation passage across independent conditioned-medium lots (n  3).

Or, capture-compatibility controls indicate that observed capture-signal loss is fully explained by assay reagent-buffer incompatibility, preventing discrimination between real epitope loss and assay interference.
human_decisions_required: Approve selection of exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer (species or label) and its qualification criteria
Select the panel of formulation buffer/excipient conditions and representative device(s) to be tested
Authorize allocation of conditioned-medium lots for the matrixed experiment
manufacturability_assessment: The proposed gate is qualitative (pass/fail) and relies on orthogonal analytics plus a spike-in control; if preserved across realistic device/formulation conditions and independent lots, it is implementable as a non-numeric identity gate to inform downstream comparability and process acceptance. Yield implications depend on fractionation choice; success would enable bounding the drug-substance as EV-enriched and justify downstream CMC resource allocation.
manufacturing_rationale: Surface-marker-based identity metrics are sensitive to process, device, and formulation exposures. Embedding a spike-in recovery control and testing through the device/formulation envelope yields an assay-based go/no-go identity gate that is directly actionable by downstream process controls (formulation selection, device acceptance, TFF envelope) and comparability workflows.
measurement_strategy: Orthogonal fraction-level assay combining: (1) multi-epitope immuno-capture on intact fractions (anti-CD63, anti-CD9, anti-CD81, TIM4/AnxA5); (2) particle counting per fraction (NTA or TRPS) to define particle-peak fractions; (3) detergent + protease/RNase protection on captured material; (4) exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer added prior to device/formulation passage and fractionation to verify recovery and membrane protection; (5) capture-compatibility buffer panels (capture reagent incubated with each formulation buffer and device rinse) to rule out assay interference. Primary outputs are qualitative pass/fail calls per lot/condition.
novelty_statement: Novel: integrates a multi-epitope intact-EV surface-phenotype capture assay with an exogenous intact-EV spike-in recovery control and explicit device/formulation passage testing to distinguish true epitope/membrane loss from assay or buffer interference—this combination (multi-epitope capture + spike-in + device/formulation challenge) and the resulting qualitative pass/fail identity gate has not previously been proposed in SGL-001 and directly addresses the selected surface-phenotype gap.
principal_risks: Spike-in tracer may not mimic endogenous EV capture behavior, invalidating the recovery control.
Capture-reagent incompatibility with certain formulation buffers could produce false negatives even after buffer-compatibility panels.
Device shear/exposure profiles in the experiment may not perfectly represent clinical device behavior.
proposed_potency_relationship: None asserted. The surface-phenotype identity gate is explicitly defined as non-potency: it discriminates EV-enrichment from secretome retention for CMC and comparability decisions but does not claim linkage to in vivo efficacy.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt a spike-in-controlled surface-phenotype identity gate defined by: (A) capture-positive signal for multiple canonical EV surface epitopes (CD63/CD9/CD81 and TIM4/AnxA5) on intact material that co-localizes with particle-count peaks in bounded fractions after device/formulation passage; and (B) loss or marked reduction of that capture signal after detergent + protease/RNase treatment (detergent sensitivity). Use preservation of this composite surface-phenotype as a qualitative identity gate (non-numeric) distinguishing an EV-enriched drug-substance candidate from secretome-retaining concentrates for downstream CMC decisions.
title: Does an orthogonal, spike-in-controlled intact-EV surface-phenotype assay that includes device/formulation passage and multi-epitope capture distinguish EV-enriched fractions from secretome concentrates?
